messages:
nina (design): quick check: proposing we add a compact 'state-preserve' toggle in the sidebar header. default ON for logged-in users. toggling OFF would make sidebar links behave as clean navigations (no filters carried). this helps power users vs new users. thoughts?

marta (ux): interesting. but we should avoid adding too many persistent controls. maybe make it contextual: show a small toggle only when there are active filters to preserve.

sam (frontend): feasible. storing preference in localStorage. urls remain canonical with params; toggle controls whether we include params when building nav links.

eli (eng): backend note: saved searches and shortlinks will still resolve independent of toggle. toggle only affects link generation in UI. also we need to ensure internal links in emails use canonical full URLs.

lina (product): analytics: track toggle usage as `nav_preserve_state=true/false`. also A/B test default ON vs default OFF for new users.

marta (ux): accessibility: when toggling OFF, we should show an inline confirmation toast: "Sidebar will stop preserving filters when navigating." with an accessible dismiss button.

nina (design): copybrain: label as "Keep view context" and tooltip "Preserve filters and active tab when switching sections". less jargon-y.

aria-bot: accessibility reminder: ensure the toggle is reachable via keyboard and exposed as checkbox role with aria-checked.

sam (frontend): small implementation note: for server-side rendered pages we need to fall back to full reload links when `preserve` is false. i'll document behaviors in the RFC.

eli (eng): edge-case: if user toggles preserve ON but has ephemeral private filters (e.g., `show_internal=true`), we should exclude those from auto-inclusion unless explicitly saved. might need a deny-list.

marta (ux): agreed. we should surface which filters are considered 'sensitive' and excluded via microcopy.

nina (design): next steps: sam to update RFC with toggle behavior, eli to draft deny-list, marta to mock where the toggle appears. follow-up in design review Thurs. :+1:
